bibl.title: The Structure and Function of Complex Networks

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The most important observation to come out of studies such as these is that networks are generally very far from random.

span.label: structure and function of complex networks
span.quote: This paper reviews recent (and some not-so-recent) work on the structure and function of networked systems such as these.

span.label: review
span.quote: Here we review developments in this field, including such concepts as the small-world effect, degree distributions, clustering, network correlations, random graph models, models of network growth and preferential attachment, and dynamical processes taking place on networks.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: generative network models - random graphs and growth with preferential attachment - reproduce the observed structure of real networks (skewed degree distributions, small-world, clustering)
span.quote: models of network growth and preferential attachment

span.label: the crucial theoretical developments in the field remain open
span.note: what this limits: the theoretical claims of the review: IT REMAINS TO BE SEEN WHAT THE CRUCIAL THEORETICAL DEVELOPMENTS WILL BE IN THIS AREA
span.quote: It remains to be seen what the crucial theoretical developments will be in this area.

span.label: The review acknowledges that the study of networks is incomplete and that only some of the described network variants are covered by the work it reviews.
span.note: what this limits: the coverage of the survey: THE STUDY OF NETWORKS IS BY NO MEANS A COMPLETE SCIENCE YET, AND MANY OF THE POSSIBILITIES HAVE YET TO BE EXPLORED IN DEPTH
span.quote: The study of networks is by no means a complete science yet, and many of the possibilities have yet to be explored in depth, but we will see examples of at least some of the variations described here in the work reviewed in this paper.

span.label: The field reviewed has no systematic programme for characterising network structure, so the measures surveyed may not be the important ones.
span.note: what this limits: every structural measure surveyed: WE DO NOT YET, AS WE DO IN SOME OTHER FIELDS, HAVE A SYSTEMATIC PROGRAM FOR CHARACTERIZING NETWORK STRUCTURE - the measures are ad hoc by the review's own account
span.quote: We do not yet, as we do in some other fields, have a systematic program for characterizing network structure.

span.label: Little can be reported on the third aim of the field - the effect of structure on system behaviour - because that work is only beginning.
span.note: what this limits: any structure-to-behaviour claim: STUDIES OF THE EFFECTS OF STRUCTURE ON SYSTEM BEHAVIOR ... ARE STILL IN THEIR INFANCY
span.quote: Studies of the effects of structure on system behavior on the other hand are still in their infancy.

span.label: The review closes by stating that the whole subject it surveys is at an early stage.
span.note: what this limits: the settledness of everything the review surveys: THE STUDY OF COMPLEX NETWORKS IS STILL IN ITS INFANCY
span.quote: The study of complex networks is still in its infancy.

span.label: The name in general use is stated to overreach: only the degree distribution is scale-free, while other properties of the same networks do have scales.
span.note: what this limits: the term scale-free network as a description of the whole network: the review states only the degree distribution is scale-free and other properties usually do have scales
span.quote: They are sometimes referred to as scale-free networks [32], although it is only their degree distributions that are scale-free;13 one can and usually does have scales present in other network properties.

span.label: Two different exponents for the same citation network were published by the same author: 2.5 to 3, then 3.04.
span.note: what this limits: a published power-law exponent for a citation network: this review records the same author revising his own value in a later paper
span.quote: He quoted a value of α = 2.5 to 3 for the exponent of his network. In a later paper he quoted a more accurate figure of α = 3.04 [344].

span.label: building the study of complex networks on the foundation of mathematical graph theory, with statistical-physics methods
span.quote: The study of networks, in the form of mathematical graph theory, is one of the fundamental pillars of

span.quote: They are sometimes referred to as scale-free networks [32], although it is only their degree distributions that are scale-free;13 one can and usually does have scales present in other network properties.

span.label: degree distribution
span.quote: Networks with power-law degree distributions have been the focus of a great deal of attention in the literature

span.label: network
span.quote: A network is a set of items, which we will call vertices or sometimes nodes, with connections between them, called edges

span.label: scale-free network - the term in general use, which the review says applies only to the degree distribution and not to the network's other properties
span.quote: They are sometimes referred to as scale-free networks [32], although it is only their degree distributions that are scale-free;13 one can and usually does have scales present in other network properties.

span.label: network - the stipulated vocabulary of the review: a set of items called vertices, with connections between them called edges
span.quote: A network is a set of items, which we will call vertices or sometimes nodes, with connections between them, called edges

span.label: qualifies → Barabási and Albert, preferential attachment
span.note: differs in: WHICH NAME THE MODEL TRAVELS UNDER, AND THE REVIEW SAYS THE EARLIER ONE DID NOT: 'The work of PRICE himself, however, is LARGELY UNKNOWN in the scientific community, and CUMULATIVE ADVANTAGE did not achieve currency as a model of network growth until its REDISCOVERY some decades later by Barabási and Albert, WHO GAVE IT THE NEW NAME OF PREFERENTIAL ATTACHMENT.' One mechanism, two names, and the currency followed the second - so a search on either name finds only half the literature
span.quote: The work of Price himself, however, is largely unknown in the scientific community, and cumulative advantage did not achieve currency as a model of network growth until its rediscovery some decades later by Barab´asi and Albert [32], who gave it the new name of preferential attachment.

span.label: contradicts → the preferential-attachment model as a model of the Web
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE MODEL'S OWN PREDICTION APPEARS IN THE DATA IT IS APPLIED TO. The model implies older vertices have higher degree; 'This correlation between degree and age has been used by Adamic and Huberman to ARGUE AGAINST THE MODEL as a model of the World Wide Web - THEY SHOW USING ACTUAL WEB DATA THAT THERE IS NO SUCH CORRELATION IN THE REAL WEB.' The refutation is of the model AS APPLIED TO THE WEB, not of the mechanism in general
span.quote: This correlation between degree and age has been used by Adamic and Huberman [4] to argue against the model as a model of the World Wide Web—they show using actual Web data that there is no such correlation in the real Web.

span.label: reinterprets → Milgram's small-world experiment
span.note: differs in: WHAT THE SAME EXPERIMENT IS EVIDENCE FOR. 'there is ANOTHER CONCLUSION that can be drawn from this experiment WHICH MILGRAM APPARENTLY FAILED TO NOTICE; it was pointed out in 2000 by Kleinberg' - roughly three decades later. The finding was in the data the whole time and needed a different question asked of it, which is the strongest kind of case for a layer that records what a result was taken to show
span.quote: However, there is another conclusion that can be drawn from this experiment which Milgram apparently failed to notice; it was pointed out in 2000 by Kleinberg

span.label: scale-free network —operationalised-as→ degree distribution
span.quote: They are sometimes referred to as scale-free networks [32], although it is only their degree distributions that are scale-free;13 one can and usually does have scales present in other network properties.

span.label: A review synthesizing complex-network science across social, information, technological, and biological networks: unifying concepts include the small-world effect, degree distributions (scale-free power laws), clustering, random-graph and preferential-attachment growth models, and dynamical processes on networks.
span.quote: Here we review developments in this field, including such concepts as the small-world effect, degree distributions, clustering, network correlations, random graph models, models of network growth and preferential attachment, and dynamical processes taking place on networks.

span.label: The same structural properties recur across otherwise unrelated systems (Internet, social, biological networks) — a common science of networks.
